newsitem.title: USA: Magna Group, new on NYSE, aims to top peers.
newsitem.headline: Magna Group, new on NYSE, aims to top peers.

text.p: Magna Group Inc, a St. Louis-based regional banking group whose stock debuts on Wednesday on the New York Stock Exchange, wants to beat peer companies on some key industry benchmarks, chairman and chief executive Thomas Andes said in an interview.

"Our peers are basically at 2.2 percent in return on assets (ROA) and 15-16 percent in return on equity (ROE)," Andes said. He said Magna is already close to the peer group in ROA and shooting for the 16-18 range in ROE.

Asked about consensus estimates that Magna will earn $2.16 per share this year and $2.33 next year, Andes said he is comfortable with those numbers and they could actually turn out to be conservative if the company meets its profitability targets.
Andes said one thing that has been hurting return on equity is excess capital, but the company has been both repurchasing shares and using cash where it can in acquisitions.
"The majority of sellers want stock because it's a tax-free exchange," Andes said.
About 85 percent of Magna's growth over the past 14 years has been via acquisitions, with the firm completing 44 deals in that period.
In early September, Magna announced an agreement to acquire Homeland Bankshares Corp, a $1.1 billion asset banking company based in Waterloo, Iowa.

Magna will issue 5.0 million common shares and $91.97 million in cash to complete the transaction. Andes said the planning process for the merger is going very well and it is expected the deal will be completed in late February.
Completion of the Homeland deal will raise Magna to a $6.6 billion asset institution, with banking branches in Missouri, Illinois and Iowa.
Andes believes industry consolidation is by no means over and Magna will be eyeing acquisition candidates in contiguous states such as Indiana and Wisconsin.
"We'd like to get bigger in Missouri," he said, noting that most of the company's assets are in Illinois.

Asked if he agreed with those in industry who say the asking prices for banks that are for sale have gotten too high, Andes said it is still possible to find acquisition candidates. But he said Magna will not do a deal if the earnings dilution cannot be recovered in 12 months.
"We've walked away from some where that hasn't been possible," he said.
Noting that Missouri has been the focus of some of the bigger bank deals of 1996, including the pending acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares Inc by NationsBank
